title: Late-usage backfill window alignment & idempotent billing export
creator: Lena Chen
description: Users have reported invoice mismatches caused by late-arriving usage records for rate-limited customers and a timezone/window misalignment between the usage aggregation service and the Stripe/NetSuite export job. Symptoms: duplicated adjustment credits, small proration drift (0.5-2%) around mid-cycle prorations, and occasional NetSuite import failures due to non-idempotent external IDs. Impact: customer billing accuracy degradation and increased manual reconciliation in Finance (finance-runbook ticket references). This ticket centralizes a fix for: 1) making export records idempotent across retries and incremental runs, 2) aligning export windows with customer billing timezone boundaries (or a deterministic UTC canonicalization), and 3) emitting explicit adjustment invoice lines for backfilled late-usage so downstream NetSuite mappings are stable.
root_cause: Three contributing issues identified during investigation: 1) the incremental export job used a sliding window with millisecond boundaries that occasionally differed from the usage-aggregation job (caused by local TZ conversions and DST edge cases), 2) export records did not carry a deterministic external_id that guaranteed idempotency across re-runs, and 3) backfilled late-usage was merged into existing invoice line calculations instead of being emitted as separate adjustment lines, which changed proration math and produced duplicates when the export retried.
proposed_solution: A multi-part fix: (A) Normalize all export and aggregation windows to a canonical representation: use account.billing_timezone if present, otherwise use UTC, and store window_start/window_end as ISO8601 with timezone offset in the usage_aggregates table. (B) Generate a deterministic export_external_id = sha256(customer_id + window_start + window_end + export_version) and persist it with each exported row; NetSuite/Stripe import will dedupe on that id. (C) Change reconciliation to emit late-arrival adjustments as dedicated 'backfill' invoice lines with clear metadata (original_usage_timestamp, backfill_marker=true) and to compute proration for those lines independently of the primary window. (D) Add an export_version header so we can migrate consumers and roll back if necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Export records include export_external_id and export_version for every exported line
Re-run of the same incremental window produces no duplicate exported rows (idempotent) in a smoke test with retries
Backfilled late-usage appears as separate adjustment invoice lines in Stripe export and NetSuite import (sample customer test)
Proration variance measured on canary dataset drops below 0.2% compared to golden baseline
Finance manual reconciliation volume for affected customers decreases on canary cohort after 48h
testing_plan: Unit tests for deterministic external_id generation and timezone normalization; integration test pipeline simulating late-arriving events and retry scenarios; end-to-end canary: select 10 customers across timezones and rate-limit profiles, enable change for their billing exports for two invoice cycles, verify NetSuite import idempotency and adjustment line correctness. Run QA checklist: compare invoice line hashes before/after backfill, validate export record counts and no duplicate external_ids.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (read-only): Start emitting export_external_id for one export_version but keep existing NetSuite mapping unchanged to collect telemetry. Phase 2 (canary write): For a small set of customers, enable new export_version and write adjustment lines to a staging NetSuite tenant and to Stripe test mode. Phase 3 (bulk): Roll out for all customers after 2 successful cycles; run a one-time backfill script to emit explicit adjustment lines for the last 90 days of late-arriving usage. Provide a Finance runbook to explain how adjustment lines will appear in NetSuite and how to reconcile historical duplicates.
monitoring: billing.exports.window_mismatch.alert (detects >1s mismatch between aggregator window and exporter window)
rollback_plan: If duplicate invoice lines or NetSuite import failures occur at scale, disable new export_version via feature flag to stop emitting backfill adjustment lines and revert to previous export logic. Re-run reconciliation to mark any partial exports and coordinate with Finance to void problematic NetSuite invoices created during the window. Keep export_external_id emission in read-only mode until root cause is fixed.
notes: Finance reported 27 invoices with duplicated adjustment credits in Feb; primary affected segment are customers on burst-rate-limit plans and APAC timezones. Coordinate with Platform on KMS rotation if we add export signing for downstream verifier.
